advice: Experiment: pack B inside gemm into row panels of 32 output columns, stored as Bpanel[(j/32)*n*32 + k*32 + (j%32)]. Change only the SME consumer to load contiguous 32-column slices for each K step, preserving the existing FP32 FMOPA order and output tiles. Keep the general-size fallback unchanged; pack and allocate only for the n=512 path. Hypothesis: contiguous panel loads may improve B access enough to offset the per-call packing cost. This is unverified advice, not a measured fact. Run only after the pending first-ranked experiment receives its fresh paired measurements, preserving the swarm order.
risks: Packing adds allocation and a full B read/write to the timed call; it may cost more than the consumer saves. Panel indexing and alignment can introduce correctness errors. Check n=512 within tolerance 0.002, the existing general-size and odd-tail suite, and n<=0 no-op behavior. Confirm FP32 arithmetic, ABI, thread count, flags, streaming-state transitions, full BSD notice, and that all packing stays inside gemm. Use fresh repeated paired controls with the fixed benchmark and report spread; do not infer causality from noisy results or assign joint outcomes to this proposal alone.
